title: Family Reunion Photo Ideas (and How to Collect Them)
description: Family reunion photo ideas: a step-by-step everyone photo, generational shots, a printable scavenger hunt, an old-photo wall, and sharing from every phone.
dek: Group shots, generational photos, a scavenger hunt, and getting every photo to Grandma.
excerpt: A step-by-step plan for the everyone photo, generational shots, a printable scavenger hunt, booth ideas, and how to collect photos from relatives on iPhone and Android.
secondary_keywords: how to share family reunion photos

faq.q: When should you take the family reunion group photo?
faq.a: Early, and on a schedule. Put the time on the invite, roughly an hour after the start, once late arrivals are in and before the big meal, the swimsuits or the first departures. Choose open shade over direct sun. If the reunion runs several days, take it on the first full day, when the most relatives are usually there.

faq.q: What should a family wear for reunion photos?
faq.a: Reunion T-shirts in one color are the simplest option and make the everyone photo look intentional. Otherwise, pick a palette such as blues and whites, ask people to skip big logos and tiny busy prints, and let each household choose within it. Keep a few spare shirts on hand for the relatives who forget.

faq.q: How do you take a big family photo without a photographer?
faq.a: Put a phone on a tripod or a steady surface a little above head height, angled slightly down, use the 1x lens, set a 10-second timer and leave a gap for yourself. Take at least ten frames, because someone blinks in almost every one, and check the shots before anyone leaves. A neighbor or a member of the venue staff can take over for a few frames.

faq.q: How can relatives without smartphones see the reunion photos?
faq.a: Print for them. A photo book, a stack of 4×6 prints of every photo they appear in, or a digital frame the family can send photos to all work without an app. Give one relative the job and a two-week deadline, because the first weeks after a reunion are when people still care enough to finish it.

faq.q: Can iPhone and Android relatives share photos in one album?
faq.a: Yes. A Google Photos shared album works on both, and Google says anyone with the link can view and add photos; test it on one relative’s phone first. Apple says iCloud shared albums on version 27 software also let friends and family join and contribute on the web without an Apple Account. For the reunion day itself, a shared camera such as Filmsera lets Android relatives join in the browser.
